prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a wooded slope rising away from the camera, with nearby ground at the bottom (roughly 0.5–2 m), tree trunks in the midground (about 2–6 m), and the house and upper slope farther away (roughly 6–15 m). Several trunks stand in front of and partially occlude the more distant vegetation and building; their brighter tones make this layering clearer than in RGB. Across the five frames, the changing viewpoint shifts the trunks laterally, while the overall distance to the slope and house appears fairly stable rather than showing a strong approach or retreat. The map is unreliable for exact metre estimates and gives inconsistent depths around foliage, sky, object boundaries, and the person, whose shape is not cleanly separated from the terrain.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map identifies two small car instances—one in the second frame and one in the fourth—and one person in the fifth frame; all are ahead of the camera wearer and far beyond arm’s reach, approximately 6–12 m away. The detections occupy different temporal frames rather than indicating that the labeled objects are simultaneously separated across one continuous scene; within their respective frames, they lie near the house-side upper slope, with the person roughly central-left in frame five. The map makes these small, partly obscured instances easier to locate than RGB, but it omits nearly all dominant spatial structures, including trees, ground, vegetation, rocks, and the house. The car labels appear especially unreliable because the corresponding RGB regions are tiny or visually ambiguous, and the person mask is incomplete and does not reveal facing direction or gaze.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects one person only in the fourth frame, ahead of the camera wearer near the upper slope and house, approximately 6–10 m away and well outside either person’s arm’s reach. The skeleton is nearly horizontal, indicating a low, bent, crouched, or leaning body configuration, with the head at the right side and the torso and limbs extending leftward; no confident hand skeleton is shown. This makes the person’s articulated body arrangement clearer than in RGB, but it does not establish whether the face or gaze is directed toward the camera wearer. The detection disappears in the other four frames despite the person being small or partly visible in nearby RGB frames, and the compressed, overlapping joints make exact limb positions, self-occlusion, motion, and approach or retreat unreliable.
